agents.reasoning: Primary-lane build, revised after the supervisor's fact-checks. (1) Company documents give the spine: rate base $56B (2025) -> $66B/$77B/$86B/$90B/$94B on the $60B base plan, $10B+ line of sight lifting the CAGR to ~13% [3]; 2026 ongoing EPS guide $4.04-4.16 reaffirmed on Aug 19 [21]; equity need $7B, 85% addressed [3]; the 10-Q shows 27.3M forward shares settling Dec-2026 to May-2027 and 42.5M Dec-2027 to Dec-2028 [1], so 662M at the horizon. (2) New lag facts from two 8-Ks: the CPUC set PSCo rates at $157M vs $356M requested on a 13-month average historical test year (ROE 9.3%, 54.5% equity) [21], and NSPM proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze offset by accelerated ITCs [20]. I trimmed earned ROE ~8-11bp in 2027-28, giving EPS $4.11/$4.455/$4.84 (FY26-28), 1.9% under FY27 consensus [15]. (3) Valuation: 17.2x (today's 0.91x relative to the 18.85x peer median [17], held because its causes persist) on NTM EPS $4.77 = $81.92; driver DCF $55.31 at 5.94% WACC (10y 5.12% [19]) with horizon net debt rebuilt from a cash-flow bridge ($50.1B, vs $44.1B straight-lined in round 1, because 2026-27 capex is front-loaded [3]); blend $76.6 at the 0.2 DCF weight, i.e. fairly priced. (4) WSJ/Anthropic [18]: ~$450B of cloud commitments (Google $111B, AWS $110B, >$160B Google TPU lease) and 'could spend $750B' are a general positive for data-center demand, mostly through Google, which is Xcel's largest data-center counterparty (Pine Island ESA [7], Abernathy backstop [8]). I dropped round 1's tracker label on Abernathy: TeraWulf's filing names Fluidstack as tenant with a Google backstop [8], TeraWulf sold its stake to a Fluidstack-led group, and Anthropic's named TeraWulf lease is in Kentucky [14], so I found no verified Anthropic load in Xcel territory. The S-1's warning about organised data-center opposition matches what is visible in MN (AG vs the Google ESA [23]) and CO. Counterparty risk sits first with the large-load tariffs' minimum bills, deposits and exit fees [12], and disputed amounts would go to rate cases. (5) On Kilian's IPO-liquidity question: Bloomberg has marketing from the week of Nov 9 and trading before Thanksgiving [22]. XEL's holders are yield/defensive and its base plan carries little data-center load [6], so a drain should hit AI-beta and 'AI power' names more. A flow-driven dip to ~$70 with the 10y stable and the Oct-29 plan intact would be a buying opportunity (~9% under fair value $76.6, plus a 3.1% yield [10]); a drop driven by the 10y above ~5.5%, a punitive MN outcome or a new wildfire is not. Thesis break $61. (6) Ladder: the engine mixture (bear $59.8 p0.25 / base $76.6 p0.55 / bull $90.4 p0.20, 13% within-scenario vol) is left-skewed because the DCF leg is very rate-sensitive in the bear, so I blend it 50/50 with a lognormal at the fair value and 18% vol (realized 19%), with 3% weight on a wildfire/regulatory crash tail near $55. Median ~$75.5. Price-only: the ~$2.40 of dividends paid before the horizon is excluded.
